rounds.text: Supreme Engineering Ltd is demonstrating explosive operational and financial momentum that warrants a re-evaluation of its growth trajectory. Compounded profit growth has accelerated dramatically, reaching 26% over 3 years and a remarkable 96% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E18]. This profit expansion is underpinned by a massive operational turnaround, with trailing twelve-month operating margins leaping by 29 percentage points to 10%, and quarterly operating margins hitting 19% in September 2026 against a negative 8% in the year-ago period [E22, E23]. Rules-based screening explicitly flags robust operational health, including year-over-year net profit growth of 145% and sales growth of 13% [E53, E54]. Furthermore, the business is successfully deleveraging while generating positive liquidity, evidenced by borrowings dropping to Rs 97.41 Cr alongside positive operating cash flow of Rs 1.27 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1.13 Cr [E27, E28, E29]. Market sentiment reflects this fundamental inflection, as evidenced by a stellar 12-month price return of 670.6% and a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, with the stock trading firmly above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E38, E39, E40]. Conceded: [E12] compounded sales growth over 10 years is -14%.

Supreme Engineering Ltd is trading at a severe valuation disconnect, highlighted by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 2 per share against a market price of Rs 6.68, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -263.0% [E33, E34]. The current share price demands an aggressive 29.8% earnings growth rate, far surpassing the 12.0% assumed in the base case, while the stock sits at the very top of its 52-week range following an unsustainable 575% one-year price surge [E21, E35, E36]. Fundamental operational realities fail to justify these heights, as demonstrated by a 5-year compounded sales growth of -19%, a low promoter holding of 33.39% that has dropped by 7.88 percentage points since September 2023, and significant structural underperformance in profitability metrics like an ROE of 0.45% and ROCE of 0.8% compared to sector benchmarks [E8, E11, E13, E31]. Furthermore, the business carries heavy financial risks including a low interest coverage ratio, high annualised volatility of 68.9%, a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -88.0%, and earnings that are inflated by Rs 2.62 Cr of other income [E41, E42, E47, E51]. conceded: [E18]

While the bear relies heavily on rigid valuation models like the DCF, it overlooks the undeniable proof of a powerful operational turnaround that outpaces historical baselines [E60]. Net profit has surged by 96% over the trailing twelve months alongside a 145% year-on-year spike, accompanied by an impressive rules-based screen score of 72 out of 100 [E18, E52, E54]. Operating margins have dramatically expanded by 29 percentage points in the TTM period to reach 10%, and quarterly operating margins jumped by 27 percentage points to 19% in September 2026 [E22, E23]. Far from being a hollow rally, the company generated positive operating cash flow of Rs 1.27 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 1.13 Cr in March 2026, while actively reducing its borrowings down to Rs 97.41 Cr by September 2026 [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, dismissing the market price ignores the absolute relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, with the stock trading firmly above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E38, E39]. conceded: [E33, E34]

While the bull celebrates a powerful operational turnaround driven by a 96% TTM profit surge and a 145% YoY net profit spike, it glosses over the fundamental reality of decelerating earnings growth and a structurally distressed core business [E18, E54, E57]. The multi-year trajectory tells a starkly different story than the recent snapshot, marked by a dismal 18.7% contraction in compounded sales growth over the past five years and a 14% decline over a decade [E12, E49]. The touted margin expansion to a 10% TTM operating margin and 19% in September 2026 masks an inconsistent yearly and quarterly trend, operating within a cyclical earnings profile that historically undermines sustainability [E22, E23, E24, E25, E46]. Furthermore, while positive operating and free cash flows of Rs 1.27 Cr and Rs 1.13 Cr respectively in March 2026 are welcome, they are fundamentally eclipsed by a massive debt load of Rs 97.41 Cr, a low interest coverage ratio flagged as negative, and an earnings profile artificially padded by Rs 2.62 Cr of other income [E27, E28, E29, E47, E51]. Finally, pointing to a relative-strength rating of 100 and a price sitting 100% of the way up its 52-week range merely confirms that expectations are running violently ahead of delivery, with recent price growth outpacing profit growth by 479% and creating an extreme vulnerability to the company's historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -88.0% [E4, E39, E41, E45]. conceded: [E18, E22, E23, E27, E28, E29, E38, E39, E52, E54]
